# New-ZbxCorrelationOperation

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a correlation operation for the -Operation of New-ZbxCorrelation and Set-ZbxCorrelation.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxCorrelationOperation [-Type] <ZabbixCorrelationOperationType> [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An operation says what a matching event correlation closes: the old problems, the new event, or both. The New-ZbxCorrelationOperation cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Operation of New-ZbxCorrelation and Set-ZbxCorrelation take as it is, alone or in an array. -Type is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build an operation that closes the old problems

```powershell
New-ZbxCorrelationOperation Old
```

-Type is positional: Old closes the open problems the new event matches, New closes the new event itself.

### Example 2: Use it in an event correlation

```powershell
$condition = New-ZbxCorrelationCondition NewEventTag -Tag 'scope'
New-ZbxCorrelation -Name 'Disaster correlation' -Filter @{ evaltype = 'AndOr'; conditions = @($condition) } -Operation (New-ZbxCorrelationOperation Old), (New-ZbxCorrelationOperation New) |
    Select-Object Name, Status
```

New-ZbxCorrelation takes the operation in -Operation, alone or with the other one.

## PARAMETERS

### -Type

What the correlation does when its conditions match: close the old events, or close the new event.
